search_log: Searched "Michael Connelly Two Kinds of Truth excerpt publisher first chapter" and opened the sustained authorized excerpt on Michael Connelly's official site.
Searched "Two Kinds of Truth Michael Connelly point of view third person narrator" and opened BookRags' whole-book point-of-view analysis.
Searched exact combinations of "Two Kinds of Truth" with "third-person", "third person limited", "point of view", and "narrator perspective"; opened Michael Carlson's explicit critical comparison.

Checked author-site announcement, audiobook, review, Google Books/Play, library, Wikipedia, and scholarly-search results; announcements, catalog copy, customer reviews, generic series claims, and unrelated truth/narrative scholarship were not used as controlling evidence.
Targeted searches found no credible indication of sustained first-person, second-person, epistolary, frame, or alternating-person sections in this novel.
person_note: The controlling narration is third-person limited through Harry Bosch. Multiple interior Goodreads passages independently show external he/Bosch narration with access to his knowledge and thoughts; dialogue and aphorisms were kept non-base, and terse or clipped passages were treated conservatively as unmarked. The authorized opening uses the same sustained third-person pattern, while two explicit whole-book sources confirm that this perspective controls the novel. No credible contrary or alternating-person structure was found; the only limitation is that the Tier A excerpt covers the opening rather than every chapter.
